scope.quote: We analyze how investors and information intermediaries perceive auditor tenure.
This study focuses on how investors and information intermediaries perceive auditor tenure.
We use earnings response coefficients (ERCs) from contemporaneous returns-earnings regressions to measure investor perceptions of earnings quality.
We analyze the perceptions of three primary users of audited financial statements: investors, independent rating agencies, and financial analysts.

Reduced models (no controls), restricted-sample estimates, Table 4 CAR-window/deflator sensitivity analyses, the unreported investment/non-investment-grade split, and minimum-analyst-count sensitivity analyses are excluded. The four selected outcomes are parallel tests of the same principal perception question, not an attempt to collect every robustness or partition result.

Every selected model uses Equation (1) with 32 actual RHS terms plus an intercept. The generic nine-control equation and term count are supported by the coordinator-verified transcription in the supplied reading. The Table 7 model uses EPS for E and absolute change in EPS for ΔE, and its nine controls substitute Analysts for Persistence.

The annual cross-sectional estimator is not named in the paper, so method remains null. Coefficients are averaged over 11 annual fits, with time-series standard errors; stock-ranking and debt-rating t-statistics involving Tenure additionally use the described autocorrelation correction.
